chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If the giver of the gift has received compensation (offset) for it, then it is not for him to retract (revoke) it.
ai.seo_question: Can a gift be revoked if the giver received compensation for it?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the condition for revoking a gift (hiba) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from a sale (bay') where compensation is inherent. It establishes that if the recipient provides a specific counter-value or offset (i'wad) to the giver, the transaction transforms into a compensated exchange, thereby barring the giver from unilateral revocation. This ruling is pivotal in distinguishing between gratuitous gifts and conditional transfers in Islamic civil law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘If the giver of the gift has offset it (against something else), so it is not for him that he can retract (from the original gift)’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a gift-giver receives something in exchange, he then cannot take back what he has given as gift.’”
